title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 133
paragraphs: So the Persians, I say, were trying to interpret the gifts. Meanwhile, the single Scythian division that had first been assigned to guard along the Maeotian lake and then to go to the Ister and come to speech with the Ionians, when they arrived at the bridge, spoke as follows: “Ionians, we have come bringing you freedom, if you are willing to listen to us. For we are informed that Darius gave you orders to guard the bridge for sixty days only, and then, if he had not come back within that time, to take yourselves off to your own land. Now, therefore, if you do as we say, you will be free from blame on his part and on ours. Stay the appointed days and then, after that, get yourselves away.” They, when the Ionians had engaged to do this, hastened back again by the quickest way.
